prompt: Find the tallest person by checking each person once.
why: You can't know who is tallest without looking at everyone, but once each is enough. One pass over n people is O(n).
trap: You don't compare everyone with everyone.

prompt: Twice as many emails takes twice as long to scan.
tells: Twice as many emails takes twice as long
why: Double the data, double the time: the work grows in a straight line with the size. That's linear time, O(n).
trap: Quadratic would be four times as long.

prompt: Search an unsorted list for a name by going through it from the start.
tells: going through it from the start
why: With no order to exploit, the name could be anywhere, so you may have to check every entry. A full scan is O(n).

prompt: Add up every number in a list.
why: Every number has to be added once, and nothing more. Touching each item once is O(n).

prompt: Find a quote in a book with no index by reading page by page.
why: Without an index there's no shortcut, so you read pages until the quote turns up. Checking items one by one is O(n).

prompt: Count how many students passed by going down the class list once.
why: You look at each student once and keep a running count. A single pass through the list is O(n).
trap: Once through, not once per student.
